items.title: Global monkey-patch of Slicer's SegmentEditorEffects class at startup

findings.title: Global monkey-patch of Slicer's SegmentEditorEffects class at startup
findings.explanation: TaranisLib/__init__.py:29-33 calls guardAutoCompleteEffect() from startupCompleted (Taranis.py:136), so the class method of Slicer's AbstractScriptedSegmentEditorAutoCompleteEffect is replaced for every Slicer user, including those who never open Taranis. Any change in Slicer's effect implementation or in other extensions that also patch this method can silently break Fill between slices / Grow from seeds, and the patch is never removed on shutdown.
findings.suggestion: Do not patch Slicer classes at startup. Report the upstream bug instead, or apply the guard only while a Taranis widget is active and restore the original method on cleanup.

items.title: scikit-image installed into Slicer's Python with full dependency resolution

findings.title: scikit-image installed into Slicer's Python with full dependency resolution
findings.evidence:
if not slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay(
            "The centerlines need the Python package scikit-image (3D thinning), which is not installed.\n\n"
            "Install it now (download from the Python package index)?", windowTitle="CBCT planning"):
        return False
    slicer.app.setOverrideCursor(qt.Qt.WaitCursor)
    try:
        slicer.util.pip_install("scikit-image")
findings.explanation: Unlike the MONAI/einops installs, this call has no --no-deps, so pip resolves scikit-image's requirements (numpy, scipy, networkx, imageio, tifffile, pillow, lazy_loader) and may upgrade or downgrade numpy/scipy that Slicer bundles, breaking Slicer or other extensions for the user. The user consents to installing scikit-image, not to changing numpy/scipy.
findings.suggestion: Install with --no-deps after checking that the dependencies are already present, or ship the thinning step without scikit-image; at minimum warn explicitly that bundled numpy/scipy may be changed.

findings.title: CBCT planning installs scikit-image with dependencies into Slicer's shared Python
findings.explanation: The user is asked to confirm, but the install is a plain pip_install with no --no-deps, so scikit-image's declared requirements (numpy/scipy/etc.) can be upgraded or changed in Slicer's shared environment and affect other extensions. The MONAI path already avoids this with --no-deps. Requirements are not pinned, so a downgrade of a bundled package is possible through transitive dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Install with --no-deps after checking that numpy/scipy/imageio/etc. are already present, or pin a compatible version range and document the change in the confirmation dialog.

items.title: Large binary images committed to the repository

findings.title: Large binary images committed to the repository
findings.explanation: banner.png (about 1.7 MB) is duplicated in four module Resources folders, and several multi-megabyte screenshots and JPEGs are in the repository root. These bloat the clone and are not needed at runtime beyond the icon and banner.
findings.suggestion: Keep one shared copy of the banner and move the large screenshots to a release asset or external URL, which EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS already references.

items.title: Licence of the downloaded AI model weights is not stated

findings.title: Licence of the downloaded AI model weights is not stated
findings.evidence:
# Release that holds the model files (upload the .pth and .txt files as release assets with these names)
MODEL_RELEASE_URL = "https://github.com/4burakfe/SlicerAether/releases/download/Trained_Models/"
findings.explanation: The extension is MIT, but the SwinUNETR weights it downloads come from a different repository (SlicerAether) and no licence or terms for those weights are given in the code or (as far as I read) the README. Users and redistributors cannot tell whether the weights may be used clinically or commercially.
findings.suggestion: State the licence/provenance of the model weights (training data, terms) in the README and next to the download.

items.title: Same torch.load pattern in the LSF calculator

findings.title: Same torch.load pattern in the LSF calculator
findings.explanation: LSFcalc loads the same weights the same way, so the same risk applies to the LSF module's model folders.
findings.suggestion: Use weights_only=True and share the verified loader between the two modules.

items.title: Taranis test suite is not registered with CTest

findings.title: Taranis test suite is not registered with CTest
findings.evidence:
if(BUILD_TESTING)
  # Register the unittest subclass in the main script as a ctest.
  # Note that the test will also be available at runtime.
  slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)
endif()
findings.explanation: Taranis/Testing/Python contains 9 test files (e.g. test_rules.py) but Taranis/CMakeLists.txt never does add_subdirectory(Testing), so those tests are neither built nor run by the extension's CI, unlike the other modules which have a Testing/CMakeLists.txt.
findings.suggestion: Add add_subdirectory(Testing) under BUILD_TESTING and register the test files, or remove the unused directory.

items.title: Tests for submodules are not registered with CTest

findings.title: Tests for submodules are not registered with CTest
findings.explanation: The per-module Testing/Python CMakeLists for LSFcalc, easy_reg, and the dosimetry modules only contain commented-out slicer_add_python_unittest calls. Only the hub has unit tests wired into the build, so regressions in those modules would not be caught by CI.
findings.suggestion: Register the existing module tests, or remove the empty test directories.

findings.title: Unbounded module-level DICOM header cache
findings.explanation: The cache is keyed by node ID and instance UIDs and is never cleared, so loading many series in a long session keeps growing it (and keeps stale entries for deleted nodes). Small leak, but it also means a volume whose DICOM header changed is never re-read.
findings.suggestion: Clear the cache on scene close or cap its size.

items.title: sys.path.append with a generic path at import time in three modules

findings.title: sys.path.append with a generic path at import time in three modules
findings.explanation: When TaranisLib cannot be imported, these modules append a Taranis folder to sys.path. This is a global side effect at import in Slicer's process and may pick up an unrelated TaranisLib package. It is only reached in the fallback branch.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the extension's CMake install, which already installs TaranisLib next to each module, or remove the fallback for release builds.

items.title: torch.load of downloaded model weights without weights_only

findings.title: torch.load of downloaded model weights without weights_only
findings.explanation: The .pth files come from a GitHub release and are unpickled by torch.load. In ai.py the download is SHA256-pinned (ai.py:172-174), which mitigates tampering, but the same pattern appears in LSFcalc/LSFcalc.py:1710 whose download path I could not verify, and on PyTorch < 2.6 the default is weights_only=False, so a replaced release asset would execute code. A user-supplied models folder (SETTING_MODELS_FOLDER) is also searched, so arbitrary local .pth files are loaded.
findings.suggestion: Pass weights_only=True to torch.load (state_dicts load fine) and verify the SHA256 in the LSFcalc download path as well.

findings.title: torch.load of model weights without weights_only
findings.explanation: Weights are loaded with torch.load(modelPath) from any file found in user-selected or module folders. The download path verifies SHA256, but files already on disk, or files placed in the custom AI models folder, are trusted without a checksum. On PyTorch versions where weights_only defaults to False, a malicious .pth can execute code on load. Exposure is limited to users who place untrusted files in those folders.
findings.suggestion: Pass weights_only=True to torch.load (state_dict only), and verify the SHA256 of local files when they match a known model name.

items.title: ~10 MB of screenshots and banners committed to the repository

findings.title: ~10 MB of screenshots and banners committed to the repository
findings.explanation: Four screenshots (~1.5 MB each), taranis_logo.png (620 KB) and four copies of banner.png (1.7 MB each) are committed, so every extension build and checkout downloads ~10 MB of images that are only used for documentation and the module panel. The automated scan also reported much larger PNG/JFIF files (7-11 MB) that I could not read.
findings.suggestion: Downscale the screenshots and banners (a few hundred KB is enough) or host them outside the build tree.

items.title: Licence of downloaded model weights not stated in what was reviewed

findings.title: Licence of downloaded model weights not stated in what was reviewed
findings.evidence: Taranis is released under the **MIT License**.
findings.explanation: The app downloads model weights from the SlicerAether release, but the licence of those weights is not stated in this repository. The extension's MIT licence covers only the code. TotalSegmentator-based liver-lesion tasks are non-commercial only, and the README and UI state this.
findings.suggestion: State the licence of the downloaded model weights (SlicerAether release) and the TotalSegmentator terms in the README.

items.title: Optional runtime dependencies (PyTorch, TotalSegmentator) not declared in EXTENSION_DEPENDS

findings.title: Optional runtime dependencies (PyTorch, TotalSegmentator) not declared in EXTENSION_DEPENDS
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA") # Specified as a list or "NA" if no dependencies
findings.explanation: AI segmentation needs the PyTorch extension (PyTorchUtils) and liver-on-MRI segmentation needs TotalSegmentator; both are optional and handled with clear messages, so this is not a defect, but declaring them would let the Extensions Manager install them.
findings.suggestion: Consider listing PyTorch and TotalSegmentator in EXTENSION_DEPENDS if they are meant to be installed with the extension.
